headline: London Laptop Prices Set to Rise 3.9% Within Months

cards.title: Satellites and Supply
cards.text: Taiwan reservoirs show stable water supplies and fab expansion, yet severe chip shortages and AI demand drive strong supply pressure of 0.394.

cards.title: London Price Impact
cards.text: Laptops jump from £1,150 to £1,194 in six months and £1,235 in twelve. High-end GPUs rise from £1,650 to £1,684.

cards.title: Buy Now Advised
cards.text: Buy now. With a 0.97 probability of laptop increases and a 0.674 chance for GPUs, prices will only climb higher.

vision_notes.text: Clearer views reveal robust green vegetation and stable reservoir water levels near 5-year norms. Stable water availability ensures uninterrupted cooling for Hsinchu fabs, supporting steady high-end GPU production.

Heavy cloud cover obscures the reservoir, though indices indicate stable water levels consistent with the five-year normal. Water supply to Tainan semiconductor fabs remains secure, posing no immediate disruption to high-end GPU manufacturing.
Dense cloud cover dominates both scenes, but a 6.8% increase in built-up density (NDBI) indicates continued semiconductor fab expansion, signaling steady or growing long-term laptop component supply.

Increased cloud cover obscures parts of the harbor, while expanding built infrastructure (elevated NDBI) and dense vessel traffic point to robust port operations, supporting steady export throughput for laptops.
